summary.tldr: Requires certain dangerous offenders and repeat first degree murder offenders to be classified and held as maximum security inmates.
what_it_does: Assigns a maximum security classification to any inmate found to be a dangerous offender or convicted of more than one first degree murder.
Requires those inmates to be confined in a maximum security penitentiary or in a maximum security area of a penitentiary.
Makes transfer decisions subject to the new maximum security rule.
Makes maximum security offenders ineligible for unescorted temporary absence.
who_it_affects: People convicted of multiple first-degree murders
summary.background: The bill amends the Corrections and Conditional Release Act. It adds a new rule for maximum security classification and updates the rules on confinement, transfers, and temporary absence.
